take_homes: Lock the judge and change only the generator. If I move the scorer, the improvement number is meaningless.
A flat score means the judge has run out of things to see. It doesn't mean the work is good, so I have to check the judge against my own reading.
I need two checks: one that the facts are tied to sources, and one that the output is useful to the person deciding.

monday.move: Run the pilot-cohort pricing brief through a generate, judge, rewrite-tactic loop with the groundedness judge, and compare its flags with my own read of 5 outputs

monday.stop_condition: Stop when flagged claims stop dropping across rounds, and I've checked the judge by hand on 5 outputs

misconception.why: The improvement came from a tactic file rewritten against a fixed judge, not from my wording a prompt better. I still think prompts matter, but the judge and loop are the bigger part.

one_line: It's worth the time for the idea that the scorer must stay fixed and that a flat score doesn't mean good, but the second half repeats itself and the 30-minute wait is mostly dead time.
